info.name: Public Sector Backend
info.description:
Full API coverage for the public-sector-backend NestJS app: Phase 1 auth (Admin/Agent/Client), the Governance Bundle (sessions, invites, audit log), and Document Ingestion Infrastructure.

Organized into four top-level groups (Admin, Agent, IPPIS, Client) plus a standalone Health check. Each group is self-contained: it has its own Auth (where applicable) and its own Session sub-folder using that group's own tokens, so you can run a whole group top-to-bottom without reaching into another group. Admin's 'Force-Revoke Sessions' (which targets an Agent's or a Client's sessions) stays under Admin since it's an admin-performed action, even though its target is an Agent/Client — it does not change how Agent/Client manage their own sessions.

Each endpoint has multiple requests: at least one success scenario and the meaningful failure scenarios (validation, auth, permission, not-found). Success requests have test scripts that capture tokens/ids into collection variables so later requests in the same folder (or run via Collection Runner) chain automatically.

MAINTENANCE: this collection must be kept in sync with the codebase. See ../CLAUDE.md and postman/README.md for the standing rule — any change to a controller, DTO, or permission key must be reflected here in the same change.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Everything authenticated as an AdminUser: login, this admin's own sessions, back-office reference routes, invite management, audit log viewing, and force-revoking an Agent's/Client's sessions.

request.description: Logs in the seeded bootstrap admin (BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD from .env).

The token is only ever sent via the (mock console) email provider, never returned by any API response — it's never captured automatically by this collection. Check the running server's console log after 'Admin > Invites > POST /admin/invites - Success' for a line like 'Email to ... Use this token to accept: <token>', then paste it into the invite_token collection variable before running this request.

exec: pm.test('status 200 or 401 (401 if invite_token was not set from server logs)', () => {

item.name: Session
item.description: Refresh/logout/session-listing for the Admin principal, using admin_access_token/admin_refresh_token.

request.description: Not role-namespaced — the Session row itself carries the principal type. Rotates the token: the old refresh token is revoked and a new one is returned.
Run 'GET /auth/sessions - Success' first to populate session_id.
Idempotent — also returns 200 on an already-revoked/unknown token.
Revokes every session for the authenticated principal. Run 'Admin > Auth > POST /auth/admin/login - Success' again afterward to get a fresh usable token, since this one's session is now revoked.

There is no GET /admin/roles endpoint yet to look up role ids. Find the SUPER_ADMIN role's id directly in the database (e.g. `SELECT id FROM "Role" WHERE name = 'SUPER_ADMIN';`) and set super_admin_role_id before running this.

exec: pm.test('status PENDING, no token in response', () => { pm.expect(json.status).to.eql('PENDING'); pm.expect(json.token).to.be.undefined; });

request.description: Run 'POST /admin/invites - Success' first to populate invite_id.

item.name: Force-Revoke Sessions
item.description: Admin-performed actions targeting an Agent's or a Client's sessions. This does not affect, and is not affected by, the Agent/Client folders' own session management of themselves.

request.description: Set agent_id to a real Agent row's id first (e.g. from the database, since there's no agent-listing endpoint yet).
Set client_id to a real Client row's id first (e.g. captured after a successful OTP verify, or from the database).
Run 'POST /admin/permissions - Success' first so this key already exists.
Run 'POST /admin/permissions - Success' first to populate permission_id.
key is immutable — only description can change.

item.name: DELETE /admin/permissions/:id - Blocked, in use by a role (409)

request.description: Run 'Admin > Roles > POST /admin/roles/:id/permissions - Success' first to assign this permission to a role.
Run 'Admin > Roles > DELETE /admin/roles/:id/permissions/:permissionId - Success' first so it's no longer in use.
Run 'POST /admin/roles - Success' first to populate role_id.
super_admin_role_id must be set first (see the Invites folder's description for how to find it).
Run 'Admin > Permissions > POST /admin/permissions - Success' and this folder's 'POST /admin/roles - Success' first.
Run the permission-removal request above first, and make sure no admin has this role assigned.
admin_id is set by 'Admin > Reference > GET /admin/me - Success'. role_id is set by 'Admin > Roles > POST /admin/roles - Success' — run that again first if you already deleted it in this run.
Only returns 409 if admin_id is genuinely the only SUPER_ADMIN holder in this environment (true on a freshly seeded database).

exec: pm.test('status 409 (or 200 if other SUPER_ADMIN holders exist)', () => pm.expect([200,409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: IPPIS
item.description: Document ingestion for the three IPPIS-related source documents (IPPIS Broadsheet, Disbursed Loans Report, Repayment Schedule) — upload, batch tracking, and snapshot/file download. These are admin-authenticated actions (no separate 'IPPIS principal' exists in the JWT system), so its Session sub-folder reuses the Admin identity — this is intentional, not a duplicate-in-error.

request.description: Attach an .xlsx file with one sheet per agency (NPF/NSCDC/IMMIGRATION/CORRECTIONAL), each with a header row containing at least "Staff ID" and "Employee Name" — rows are upserted into IppisRecord by (agency, staffId). Do NOT attach the real sample files under docs/added/ to a shared workspace — those contain real BVNs/bank data and are gitignored for that reason.

formdata.description: Month 13 does not exist — must match YYYY-MM with month 01-12

request.description: Run 'POST /admin/documents/ippis-broadsheet/upload - Success' first to populate ippis_batch_id. Note the batch reaches COMPLETED asynchronously via the BullMQ worker — if you run this immediately, status may still show PENDING/PROCESSING; wait a second and retry if so.

file_storage_key must be URL-encoded (storage keys contain '/', e.g. 'uploads/ippis_broadsheet/171...-broadsheet.xlsx') — Postman encodes path variables automatically, but if pasting manually into the raw URL, encode '/' as %2F. Populated automatically by 'GET /admin/documents/batches/:id - Success'.

item.name: Session (admin identity)
item.description: Document ingestion has no principal type of its own — it's authenticated as an Admin. Identical mechanics to Admin > Session, included here so this group is self-contained for anyone testing just the IPPIS area. Uses admin_access_token/admin_refresh_token/session_id, same as Admin > Session.

request.description: Not role-namespaced — the Session row itself carries the principal type. Rotates the token: the old refresh token is revoked and a new one is returned.
Idempotent — also returns 200 on an already-revoked/unknown token.

item.name: Client
item.description: Everything authenticated as a Client (phone + OTP) — in this codebase, an IPPIS civil servant is onboarded and logs in as a Client. Login/OTP and this client's own session management. Independent of Admin's ability to force-revoke this client's sessions (see Admin > Force-Revoke Sessions).

request.description: The mock ConsoleOtpProvider logs the 6-digit code to the running server's stdout (e.g. 'OTP for +234...: 123456') since there's no real SMS vendor wired in. Copy that code into client_otp_code before running the verify request.
Requires client_otp_code to be set from the server console log first (see the 'otp/request - Success' request's description).

exec: pm.test('status 200 or 401 (401 if client_otp_code was not set from server logs)', () => {
